title: A theory of learning data statistics in diffusion models, from easy to hard
claim: Models learn simple low-order statistics first and higher-order structure later, visible as staged loss curves and sample quality over training.
layout: 3 loss plots on top, 4 sample grids below, left-to-right by training step
description: The top row has three line plots of loss against training steps on a log x-axis. Panel a) shows CIFAR10 overall loss, with train and test curves (dashed dark red and pink) falling sharply. Blue 'mean' and 'mean + cov.' clone curves drop early, then plateau or rise. Gray vertical dotted lines mark the training stages. Panel b) shows CIFAR10 at a fixed noise level. The mean-clone loss rises well above the train/test loss, with shaded standard-deviation bands. Panel c) shows the mixed cumulant model, where the mean and mean+cov. curves fall and then separate slightly from the test loss. The bottom row, d) to g), has 3x3 grids of generated CIFAR-like images at steps 10, 1152, 12068 and 100000. They go from pure noise to blurry blobs, then to coherent object shapes. The eye goes first to the loss curves, then to the sample progression.
caption: Sequential learning in diffusion models. a) Test loss of diffusion model and loss on CIFAR-10 clones during training. Vertical dotted lines mark training stages of images generated from the model shown in panels d)-g). All curves are averages over 3 initializations of the network models and $5\cdot10^3$ test data. Shaded areas report standard deviation over random initialization. Panel b) reports the same as a), but for denoising samples with fixed level of noise $x=e^{-t}x_0+\sqrt{1-e^{-2t}}z$ where $x_0$ is a data point and noise $z \sim \stdGauss$. c) Test loss of a neural network trained on the mixed cumulant model with dimension $d=10^2$ a fixed level of noise, evaluated on clones of the data set. All curves in panel c) are averages over $5 $ initializations of the network model and $10^4$ test data. d)-g) Samples generated from U-nets [ref] on CIFAR-10 at various training stages.
abstract: While diffusion models have emerged as a powerful class of generative models, their learning dynamics remain poorly understood. We address this issue first by empirically showing that standard diffusion models trained on natural images exhibit a distributional simplicity bias, learning simple, pair-wise input statistics before specializing to higher-order correlations. We reproduce this behaviour in simple denoisers trained on a minimal data model, the mixed cumulant model, where we precisely control both pair-wise and higher-order correlations of the inputs. We identify a scalar invariant of the model that governs the sample complexity of learning pair-wise and higher-order correlations that we call the diffusion information exponent, in analogy to related invariants in different learning paradigms. Using this invariant, we prove that the denoiser learns simple, pair-wise statistics of the inputs at linear sample complexity, while more complex higher-order statistics, such as the fourth cumulant, require at least cubic sample complexity. We also prove that the sample complexity of learning the fourth cumulant is linear if pair-wise and higher-order statistics share a correlated latent structure. Our work describes a key mechanism for how diffusion models can learn distributions of increasing complexity.
